items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the powers of the New York state bridge authority
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6019

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the powers
of the New York state bridge authority


 PURPOSE :

This bill would authorize the New York State Bridge Authority
("Authority") to accept ownership of the Poughkeepsie-Highland
railroad bridge, which will be known as the "Walkway over the Hudson
Bridge."

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would set forth legislative findings.

Section 2 of the bill would add a new subdivision, Public Authorities
Law ("PAL") § 526(7-b), which defines the Poughkeepsie-Highland
railroad bridge as "Walkway over the Hudson Bridge".

Section 3 of the bill would amend PAL § 526(9) to add Walkway over the
Hudson to the term "bridges".

Section 4 of the bill would add a new subdivision, PAL § 528(1-b),
authorizing the Authority to accept the Walkway over the Hudson Bridge
and incidental roads, approaches, structures and facilities.

Section 5 of the bill would add a new subdivision, PAL § 528(1-c),
authorizing the Authority to accepts gifts.

Section 6 of the bill would amend PAL § 528(8) to prohibit the tolling
of the Walkway over the Hudson Bridge.

Section 7 of the bill would add a new subdivision, PAL § 528(17),
authorizing the Authority to enter into a lease or operating agreement
with the Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP)
for oversight over the deck of the bridge where a state park would be
maintained. The Authority would be responsible for maintaining the
superstructure of the Walkway over the Hudson Bridge.

Section 8 of the bill would amend PAL § 529(2) to authorize
municipalities to dedicate real property, or easements, to the
Authority.

Section 9 provides for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

PAL Title 2 authorizes the Authority to maintain five bridges: (1)
Franklin Delano Roosevelt Mid-Hudson Bridge; (2) Rip Van Winkle
Bridge; (3) Bear Mountain Bridge; (4) Hamilton Fish Newburgh-Beacon
Bridge; and (5) Kingston-Rhinecliff Bridge.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

None.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The Poughkeepsie-Highland railroad bridge spans the Hudson River and
connects the City of Poughkeepsie in Dutchess County with the Town of
Lloyd in Ulster County. The first cornerstone was laid in 1873 and the
bridge opened in 1888. The bridge is 6,767 feet long (approximately
1.25 miles). The top of the bridge deck is 212 feet above the water
and the width expands from 24 feet over land, to 35 feet over the
Hudson River (it is higher than the Brooklyn Bridge).  At the time it
was built it was one of the longest bridges in the world. During World
War II, over 3,500 train cars crossed the bridge daily. The bridge
went out of service in 1974. It is listed on the State and National
Registers of Historic Places.

The bridge currently is owned by the not-for-profit organization
Walkway Over the Hudson which is converting the bridge to a free,
pedestrian-only bridge which will provide public access to the Hudson
River's scenic landscape for pedestrians, hikers, joggers, bicyclists,
and people with disabilities. It will also connect with an extensive
network of rail-trails, parks and communities on both sides of the
river. This bill will allow OPRHP to operate the public park on the
bridge while the Authority will be responsible for maintaining the
superstructure. When completed in the Fall of 2009, it will be the
longest pedestrian bridge in the world and will be a legacy of the
Hudson- Fulton-Champlain Quadricentennial commemoration.

An independent economic impact study has concluded that the Walkway
over the Hudson bridge will generate an estimated $14.6 million
annually in new direct spending by visitors to Dutchess and Ulster
Counties. These expenditures will result in a total of $21 million per
year of new economic activity regionally and statewide.  Construction
activity on the bridge will result in the creation of 258 new jobs. In
addition, it is expected the bridge will generate $1.3 million
annually in new overall tax revenue to local, county and state
governments.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

OPRHP estimates that there will be a fiscal impact of $295,000 to
operate and maintain the "public" portion of the Walkway. This would
support 3 staff, seasonal staff and associated non-personal service
costs associated with the Walkway over the Hudson's operations and
would generally include the portions of the bridge to which the public
would have access. These resources will be secured from the OPRHP
budget. Additionally, the Authority will incur costs of approximately
$2.1 million per year over the next five years to maintain and support
the superstructure of the Walkway over the Hudson Bridge, the land
below the bridge and any other lands transferred.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The act takes effect immediately upon enactment.

summary: Relates to the New York state bridge authority; provides for the walkway over the Hudson bridge to mean the Poughkeepsie-Highland railroad bridge which was constructed across the Hudson river north of the Franklin Delano Roosevelt Mid-Hudson bridge.
